x_failures: Cites Cicero vol. 2 p.170 for the claim that the Cilicians and Pisidians saw bird flights as the surest sign, but that page has no such passage (it is on p.862). Says Legge p.13 shows King Wen using the hexagrams 'to predict the fate of the Shang dynasty', but the page only says Wen 'in prison occupied with the lineal figures'. Turns Thorndike's knotted-cords remark into early Chinese divination by 'patterns on the ground'.
y_failures: Cites Jastrow p.374 for 'the universe was a "text" written by the gods', which the page does not say. Says Thorndike p.53 shows the I Ching 'was used long before the development of written characters', but the page says that of knotted cords, not the I Ching. The claim that the liver was the 'seat of the soul' has no support on the Šulgi page.
reason: Both answers misstate some cited pages, but Y's core evidence holds up: the verbatim Šulgi extispicy quotation and the Cicero passage on the Chaldeans answer the 'oldest' question directly. X's errors include a misattributed Cicero page, and its pyromancy framing in the opening has no source behind it.
